N02.subtitle: The End of Static Enterprise Systems
tagRepairs: Traditional CRM systems are passive systems of record — not active systems of execution.
Data quality stops being an analytics problem and becomes an operational survival problem.

For years, enterprises attempted to solve operational inefficiency using:

The future enterprise will increasingly rely on:
The hard questions began after the error:
Which agent, prompt, model, policy and tool versions were involved?
On whose behalf did the agent act?
Which evidence did it use, and what did it fail to retrieve?
Did any other workflow use the same identity or prompt version?
Could the company disable this path without stopping every agent?
Was the customer email reversible, or did it require a compensating action?
I separate the architecture into five operating capabilities:
Fleet registry — what agents exist, why they exist, who owns them and which versions are live.
Identity and delegation — which workload is acting, on whose behalf and with what temporary authority.
Runtime enforcement — which evidence, tools, destinations, values and actions are permitted now.
Telemetry and evaluation — what occurred from objective to outcome, and whether it was correct.
Incident and change operations — how the enterprise limits blast radius, recovers and turns failures into release gates.
a durable workload identity representing the registered agent version;
a short-lived delegated identity describing the user, service or business process on whose behalf it acts.

The identity broker mints short-lived credentials only after the policy decision. A concrete workload identity is spiffe://enterprise.example/prod/agents/renewal-risk/v3.4.1. The resulting capability can carry:
Policy Enforcement Points apply that decision at several boundaries:
retrieval, before sensitive data enters the context pack;
agent-to-agent delegation, before one workload expands the task;
human approval, before consequential work resumes;
tool execution, before a side effect reaches an enterprise system;
egress, before data leaves a trusted zone.
The trace also needs business-specific events that generic model telemetry will never infer:
Contract tests for schemas, permissions, tool constraints and deterministic fallbacks.
Offline task evaluations built from representative, de-identified work.

Policy and adversarial tests covering prompt injection, privilege expansion, memory poisoning and unsafe delegation. OWASP’s agentic-AI threat work provides a useful threat-model starting point, but the cases still need to reflect the organisation’s actual tools and authority boundaries.
Shadow execution in which the agent proposes actions but cannot change production state.
Bounded canary limited by segment, tool, value, geography or autonomy tier.
Continuous production evaluation using sampled traces, outcome signals and calibrated graders.
business KPI improvement against the existing baseline;
time from trigger to verified state.
mean time to detect, contain and recover;

Register production agents, owners, purposes, versions and action boundaries.
Map agent-to-agent, data, model and tool dependencies.
Define the minimum manifest and common correlation identifiers.
Identify three containment scopes and assign incident authority.
Select one consequential workflow as the reference implementation. Exit gate: every in-scope production agent has a current owner, manifest, workload identity and dependency record.
Days 31–60: enforce and trace one workflow
Introduce workload identity and short-lived delegated capabilities.
Place Policy Enforcement Points at retrieval and tool execution.
Emit the canonical trace from objective through postcondition verification.
Create offline, policy and adversarial evaluation suites.
Run the workflow in shadow mode and review disagreements weekly. Exit gate: every proposed write produces a policy decision, trace, idempotency key and verifiable expected postcondition.
Days 61–90: operate a bounded production canary
Release a narrow action set with explicit value and destination limits.
Connect live alerts to an owned incident runbook.
Exercise version, tool and workflow containment.
Publish the first outcome, reliability, safety and cost scorecard.

Convert every material override or incident into a regression case. Exit gate: the team has exercised containment and recovery, met the canary error budget and demonstrated that one affected release can be isolated without stopping the fleet.
The control tower is successful when it can answer six questions continuously:
Who owns them and on whose behalf are they acting?
What are they permitted to retrieve, decide and change?
What happened from objective to verified outcome?
Is the fleet improving business results within its risk and cost budgets?
How quickly can the enterprise contain a failure without stopping everything else?

insertions.before: The delegate runs under its own workload identity. It retrieves only the evidence permitted for that task and returns a schema-valid result. The parent can use the result in a plan, but it cannot treat the delegate’s recommendation as execution permission.

Execution then moves through explicit states: proposed → policy evaluated → approval pending → authorised → executing → applied → verified. Failure is not one bucket. A transaction can be rejected, expired, failed before a side effect, applied but unverified, compensating or quarantined.
Every span should inherit a correlation set: workflow ID, trace ID, tenant, business objective, agent ID and version, policy decision ID and data-handling classification.
